flat3_contracts_counterfactual.method: Entry-level (grouped by original buy_ts) linear per-contract P&L scaling: counterfactual_qty = min(actual_qty, 3); counterfactual_pnl = (actual_pnl / actual_qty) * counterfactual_qty. APPROXIMATE -- ignores exit-ladder nonlinearity (TP1 sells 66.7% of position: qty3 sells 2/keeps 1 riding, qty5 sells 3/keeps 2 riding -- runner optionality is NOT the same shape at different qty, so this likely overstates smaller-size benefit on choppy days and understates larger-size benefit on trend days). Uses REAL fills-ledger prices throughout (not a walker/bar-replay simulation), so it does not carry the WALKER-FULL-POPULATION-ANCHOR magnitude-fidelity caveat -- the only approximation here is the linear-scaling assumption itself, disclosed above.
flat3_contracts_counterfactual.population: 222 reconstructed entries since 2026-08-06 (matched FIFO legs grouped back to their originating buy fill)

safe-2.note: already at min_contracts=3 floor essentially every entry -- flat-3 changes nothing

flat3_contracts_counterfactual.conclusion: Small, mixed, sign-uncertain effect (no CI computed on the delta -- flag as a point estimate only). Flat-3 would have cost bold-2 and risky-1 money (their tiered upsizing above 3, mostly to their min_contracts=5 floor, correlates with bigger wins as much as bigger losses in this sample) but helped risky-3 and especially safe-3 (whose few above-3 entries -- ELITE-tier upsizes to 5 -- were disproportionately its losers). Net book effect is a small positive (+$320 of +$1,040, +31%) but this is not a validated result: no bootstrap CI, small n on the qty>3 subset per arm, and the linear-scaling approximation's known bias runs in the direction of UNDERSTATING what bigger size buys on trend days -- so this number should not be read as 'shrink the ladder', only as 'sizing above the floor has not obviously paid for itself yet, arm-by-arm and outside a validated pre-registered test'.

entry_rule_diversification_design_note.method: Day-summed actual (breakout, walked) vs retest-variant (walked) P&L, 15 comparable trading days 2026-08-06..2026-09-02, same population/exit engine both sides (see H10 report for full methodology and fidelity caveats -- SIGN-ONLY except safe-2)
entry_rule_diversification_design_note.conclusion: NOT A RESULT -- a design note only. Diversifying arms by entry-TIMING rule (breakout vs wait-for-retest) does NOT meaningfully decorrelate the book: both variants read the identical trigger_level off the identical shared signal, so both are driven by the same underlying day-type (trend vs chop) that SYNTHESIS.md names as the actual mechanism. Correlation between the two entry styles' daily P&L is 0.74-0.95 depending on zone width -- higher than the 0.48-0.90 range measured BETWEEN the current 5 arms themselves (which differ by sizing/gates/stop, not entry rule). A genuine diversification lever would need a different signal source (different setup family, different instrument, different timeframe), not a different entry-timing variant of the same RIDE_THE_RIBBON trigger. This is consistent with C1/MAP.md's standing finding that current arms 'differ only in sizing, gates and exit shape... that is also why they lose together.'
